About the Small Commercial Tax Credit

The Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program accepts applications for small commercial projects to help strengthen Maryland’s communities and encourage local economic growth.  

Qualifying projects:

  • may receive a state income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses (capped at $50,000 in a 24 month period)
  • must have between $5,000 (minimum) and $500,000 (maximum) in eligible rehabilitation expenses
  • must meet all eligibility requirements described in the "Eligibility" section below

Projects in a qualified Opportunity Zone (1 or 2) may be eligible for additional state tax credits. Large or complex rehabilitation projects will benefit from early (pre-application) consultation with tax credit staff.

This page provides an overview of key steps in the process. For complete information about requirements, please review the application instructions - PDF - 9.14 MB. 

To discuss your project with Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) staff, please email us. 

Timeline

Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis until the program’s annual $2 million funding cap is reached. Applicants are encouraged to contact MHT early in the planning process for large or complex projects.  

Determination time may vary depending on the clarity of the submission and project complexity. Once applicants have their materials ready, the process typically takes about: 1 business day to complete the application, followed by a 10–30 day review for completeness and a final determination within 40–45 days after a complete application is received. There have been no recent updates to the application form.

Emergency situations

Emergency situations: If you wish to use the small commercial tax credit to assist with emergency repairs, please contact tax credit staff to discuss your project before you begin any emergency work (see below for contact details).

Eligibility 

Eligible projects for the small commercial tax credit may not exceed $500,000 for all qualified expenses. If you are planning a larger project, please consider the competitive commercial tax credit. 

Applications must meet all eligibility requirements to receive a tax credit, and all work must be approved by MHT for consistency with the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation before a project begins.  

Eligible applicants 

  • Owners of income-producing historic buildings, including commercial and mixed-use properties
  • Owners of properties that will be sold to homeowners after rehabilitation may also qualify under certain conditions

Eligible properties 

To be eligible for the tax credit, a building must be:

  1. A certified historic structure, and

  2.  At least one of the following: 

    1. Primarily income-producing, or 

    2. Rehabilitated as part of a development project to be sold to a homeowner, or 

    3. Rehabilitated for a commercial use (which can include use by nonprofits) 

A certified historic structure is a property that is: 

  • Individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, or
  • A contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, or
  • Locally designated (as an individual landmark or contributing structure) and determined by MHT to be eligible for the National Register 

Some properties located in (and certified as contributing to) a Maryland heritage area may be eligible for this program. If you are considering applying for one of these properties, please contact staff.  

Eligible projects 

The small commercial tax credit supports repairs or changes that bring a historic property to functional use while protecting important historical, architectural, or cultural parts of the building, site, and surroundings. 

Any work begun prior to MHT review and approval will not qualify for the tax credit and may jeopardize the credit for the entire project. All work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation. 

Examples of eligible projects

Eligible projects include, but are not limited to:  

  • Roof repair or replacement
  • Chimney repair and relining
  • Structural repairs
  • Window and door restoration
  • New storm doors/windows
  • Masonry repair or repointing
  • Mechanical, electrical, and plumbing work
  • Interior finish restoration, including plaster, flooring, or trim
  • Professional design, architectural, or engineering fees related to the project
  • Tool/equipment rental
  • Repair of historic outbuildings 

Ineligible projects

The following work typically does not qualify for the homeowner tax credit: 

  • Landscaping, sidewalks, patios, or parking areas
  • Repair of non-historic outbuildings
  • New construction (includes additions, expansions, or construction of new buildings on site)
  • Work that is primarily remodeling in nature
  • Appliances
  • Carpeting over historic flooring
  • Curtains, blinds, rugs, or other interior décor
  • Tool/equipment purchases
  • Pest control, chimney cleaning, drain cleaning, etc. 

Please contact MHT with any questions about eligible expenses before you begin your application.  

Using the state tax credit with federal and local tax credits 

Property owners may use the state historic tax credit with federal and local historic tax credits, if local tax credits are available and the project meets the eligibility requirements for all programs. Federal applications are reviewed by MHT in coordination with the National Park Service and should be submitted simultaneously for a streamlined review. 

However, MHT review is independent of local review and may not be waived or substituted with local tax credit approval.  

Please contact your county or municipality for more information about local tax credits. 

Three-part application process

The tax credit application has three parts: 

  1. Part 1 describes the property and its historic significance for evaluation by MHT.
  2. Part 2 describes the proposed rehabilitation work for approval.
  3. Part 3 documents the completed project for final certification. 

To get started, read the small commercial application instructions and all supporting materials. 

MHT reviews each part of the application, including documentation of the completed project (Part 3), for eligibility prior to tax credit approval.

If your project changes or you want to add new work, you must submit an amendment form. It must be reviewed and approved by MHT before starting the work for it to be eligible for the credit. You can submit as many amendments as needed during the 24-month period.
